question.knowledge_point: Evaluating a Limit at Infinity: Infinite Solutions
question.worked_solution:
First, we divide both the numerator and the denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{3}.$ Then, by noting that the reciprocals shrink to $0$ in the limit, we can then evaluate the resulting expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\,\frac{3{x}^{4}+2}{{x}^{3}-7x} & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\,\frac{(\frac{3{x}^{4}}{{x}^{3}}+\frac{2}{{x}^{3}})}{(\frac{{x}^{3}}{{x}^{3}}-\frac{7x}{{x}^{3}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\,\frac{(3x+\frac{2}{{x}^{3}})}{(1-\frac{7}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\,\frac{(3x+0)}{(1-0+0)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\,3x \\  & =\infty .\end{aligned}
$$
